text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.7% today, bouncing back after a rough two weeks that saw the stock down 7.5%. The recovery came as oil prices stabilized: US crude held around $99.64 per barrel while Brent stayed above $100, supported by continued uncertainty over Middle East tensions despite President Trump's comments suggesting the Iran conflict could wind down "fairly soon." After dropping to $134.47 just two days ago, the stock's climb back toward $138 reflects the market's relief that oil hasn't collapsed on peace hopes.

The stock's two-week decline mirrors the broader oil sector's nervousness about what lower geopolitical risk means for prices. While Trump has signaled an end to conflict is near, his own Secretary of State said Iran negotiations remain unproductive, creating conflicting signals about whether crude will stay supported or face downward pressure. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, each dollar swing in crude prices directly affects profit margins, so today's stabilization in the $100+ range gave the stock room to recover.
